issue: What must a defendant show to establish that a Rule 11(b)(3) error in the factual basis for a guilty plea affected substantial rights on plain-error review: a reasonable probability that, but for the error, he would not have pleaded guilty, or only that the record as a whole fails to supply a sufficient factual basis?
provision: Fed. R. Crim. P. 11(b)(3); Fed. R. Crim. P. 52(b)

sides.position: A defendant must show a reasonable probability that, but for the Rule 11 error, he would not have entered the guilty plea (Dominguez Benitez standard).
cases: United States v. Bryant, 976 F.3d 165 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Castro-Trevino, 464 F.3d 536 (5th Cir. 2006)
United States v. Monzon, 429 F.3d 1268 (9th Cir. 2005)
United States v. Dominguez Benitez, 542 U.S. 74 (2004)

sides.position: A defendant need only show that the record as a whole fails to provide a sufficient factual basis to support the guilty plea.
cases: United States v. Carillo, 860 F.3d 1293 (10th Cir. 2017)

quote: There is some disagreement among our sister circuits as to what is required to satisfy this standard in the context of a Rule 11(b)(3) challenge to the sufficiency of a guilty plea's factual basis.
cite: United States v. Nicole Schuster, No. 24-2942 (3rd Cir. 2026)
